'causes' and 'action' are Wattlyst's own plain-English summary of each manual's troubleshooting entry (rewritten 2026-10-21, audit Phase 8 WL-216: no manual text is quoted); the facts come from the linked manual and page reference. call_installer=true where the manual says to contact dealer/service/repair center or the fix needs DC/AC wiring work.
_meta.installer_flags: call_installer set to true on 2026-10-14 (engineer review) wherever the manual's remedy needs wiring, terminal, protection-setting or part replacement work.
_meta.heading_note: heading = the short brand and series name used in the page H2 "<heading> error codes" (audit WL-210, 21 Oct 2026); name and models are printed in the line under it.

brands.name: Growatt SPF (off-grid / hybrid 'ES' series)
brands.heading: Growatt SPF off-grid and hybrid
brands.models: SPF 3000-6000 ES / ES PLUS (codes table from SPF 6000 ES PLUS manual; same numbering family as other SPF units but verify per model)
brands.manual_note: Growatt's own manual hosted by distributor Offgridtec (b2b.offgridtec.com); fetched and read 2026-10-13/14.

codes.causes: The cooling fan has stopped or is faulty.
codes.action: See that every fan turns freely and is not choked with dust. If a fan is dead it has to be replaced, which is installer work.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: A part inside the inverter has gone above its safe temperature (about 100 °C).
codes.action: Make sure air can flow around the unit and the room is not too hot, and clear dust from the vents. A loose temperature-sensor plug can also cause it; if the code repeats, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.meaning: Battery voltage is too high (battery over-charged)
codes.causes: The battery voltage has risen too high, meaning the battery is being over-charged.
codes.action: Restart the unit. Have the installer check that the battery type, number of batteries and charge settings match the inverter; if it happens again the unit goes to the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.meaning: Battery voltage / SOC is too low (low battery)
codes.causes: The battery voltage, or the lithium battery's state of charge, has fallen too low.
codes.action: Measure the battery voltage at the inverter's DC input (or read the SOC on the screen for lithium) and let the battery recharge from solar or grid.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: The AC output is short-circuited.
codes.action: Switch off the loads and look for a faulty appliance or a wiring fault on the output side. If the fault stays with the loads off, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.meaning: Output voltage abnormal (too high / too low)
codes.causes: The inverter's output voltage has gone outside its normal band (far above or below mains voltage).
codes.action: Reduce the load and restart. If the code repeats, the unit needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: The load has been above the inverter's rating (about 110%) for longer than it allows.
codes.action: Switch some appliances off so the load is below the inverter's rated power.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage is too high. With a lithium battery that has no communication cable, the charge voltage settings (programs 19 and 21) may be set too high for that battery.
codes.action: Have the installer check the battery voltage settings, then restart. If the code repeats, the unit needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.meaning: Bus soft start failed / inverter soft start failed / current sensor failed
codes.causes: An internal start-up stage or current sensor has failed.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if the code comes back, the unit needs the maker's service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: In a parallel system, the inverters do not all see the same grid input.
codes.action: Parallel systems only: the installer should check that every inverter's AC input wiring is connected properly.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: In a parallel system, the input phase order is wrong.
codes.action: Installer work: the input phase wiring (S and T) has to be swapped.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: In a parallel system, an output phase is missing or set up wrongly.
codes.action: Installer work: all units must have the same parallel setting (single or three-phase, and phase position), and every unit must be switched on.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: The lithium battery is not talking to the inverter.
codes.action: Check the communication cable between the battery and the inverter and that the battery (BMS) protocol chosen in the settings matches the battery.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: An over-current or surge was detected.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if the code comes back, the unit needs the maker's service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage is too low.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if the code comes back, the unit needs the maker's service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.meaning: Output voltage is unbalanced / over DC voltage in AC output
codes.causes: The output voltage is unbalanced, or DC voltage has appeared on the AC output.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if the code comes back, the unit needs the maker's service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: The battery connection is open: a loose cable or a blown fuse. With a lithium battery without communication, the voltage settings (programs 19 and 21) may be too high for that battery.
codes.action: Check the battery cables and fuse (switch off first; a battery can deliver very high current). If the battery is connected properly, restart; if the code repeats, the unit needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: Power is flowing backwards into the output. Usual causes: the AC output is connected to the grid input, parallel units have different settings (program 8), current-sharing cables are loose, or the neutrals of parallel units are not joined.
codes.action: These are wiring checks for the installer. If they are all correct and the code stays, contact the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.causes: The solar (PV) input voltage is above the inverter's limit. The manual lists the code without further detail.
codes.action: The installer must check the panel string voltage against the inverter's maximum PV input.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Fault Reference Code table (p. 35)

codes.causes: Internal communication between the inverter's boards has failed. The manual lists the code without further detail.
codes.action: Treat it like other internal faults: Restart the inverter; if the code comes back, the unit needs the maker's service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Fault Reference Code table (p. 35)

codes.causes: Parallel communication has been lost (CAN fault or host lost).
codes.action: Installer work: check the parallel communication cables and that the parallel setting (program 23) is right. If it stays, contact the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Trouble Shooting table (pp. 41-42)

codes.meaning: Fan is locked when inverter is on
codes.causes: The fan has stopped while the inverter is running (warning only).
codes.action: Clean dust or anything blocking the fan; if it stays stopped, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.causes: The inverter is running hot (warning only).
codes.action: Reduce the load and improve ventilation; see Fault 02.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.causes: The battery is being over-charged (warning only).
codes.action: Have the installer check the battery charge settings (see Fault 03).
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.causes: The load is above the inverter's rating (warning only).
codes.action: Switch some appliances off.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.causes: The inverter is cutting its output power to protect itself, usually because of heat or a high PV voltage.
codes.action: Reduce the load and keep the unit cool. The manual gives no further detail.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.meaning: Solar charger stops due to low battery
codes.causes: The solar charger has stopped because the battery is too low.
codes.action: Let the battery recharge, from the grid if needed, and check its condition.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.meaning: Solar charger stops due to high PV voltage
codes.causes: The solar charger has stopped because the PV voltage is too high.
codes.action: The installer must check the panel string configuration.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.meaning: Solar charger stops due to overload
codes.causes: The solar charger has stopped because it is overloaded.
codes.action: Reduce the charging or load demand.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.causes: The battery is disconnected.
codes.action: Check that the battery breaker is on and the cables are tight; if unsure, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.causes: There is not enough solar power for the demand.
codes.action: Normal in low sun, early morning, evening or cloud; no action needed.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.causes: The battery's management system (BMS) has stopped communicating.
codes.action: Check the BMS cable and protocol setting (see Warning 20).
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

codes.meaning: Lithium battery BMS alarms: 34 Cell over voltage, 35 Cell under voltage, 36 Total over voltage, 37 Total under voltage, 38 Discharge over voltage, 39 Charge over voltage, 40 Discharge over temperature, 41 Charge over temperature, 42 Mosfet over temperature, 43 Battery over temperature, 44 Battery under temperature, 45 System shut down
codes.causes: These alarms come from the lithium battery's own management system (cell or pack voltage, temperature, or a protective shutdown).
codes.action: The fault is in the battery, not the inverter: contact the battery supplier or installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt SPF 6000 ES PLUS User Manual v1.0, Warning Indicator table (p. 36)

brands.name: Growatt MIN / MOD on-grid (TL-X family)
brands.heading: Growatt MIN and MOD on-grid
brands.models: MIN 2500-6000TL-X (manual read); MOD/MID share the Error 2xx/4xx numbering family per Growatt but only MIN TL-X was verified
brands.manual_note: Growatt manual GR-UM-155-A-04 (2022-06) hosted by distributor Offgridtec; the local copy read was the same revision (header 'GR-UM-155-A-04'). Grid-side codes (grid voltage/frequency 'Error 300-series') were not in the extracted table slice; only the entries above are verified.

codes.causes: An electric arc has been detected on the DC (solar) side.
codes.action: Switch the inverter off and have the installer check the panel connectors, then restart. If it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: Leakage current to earth is too high.
codes.action: Restart the inverter. If the code stays, contact Growatt or the installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The DC surge protection device is not working.
codes.action: After shutdown the installer should check the DC surge protector; if the code stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: A short circuit was found on PV input 1 or 2.
codes.action: The installer should check the panel polarity and restart. If the warning stays, Growatt service replaces the power board.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The dry-contact (relay output) function is not working.
codes.action: After shutdown the installer should check the dry-contact wiring; if the code stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The boost circuit for PV input 1 or 2 is damaged.
codes.action: Restart. If the warning stays, Growatt service replaces the power board.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: Too much current is being drawn through the USB port.
codes.action: Unplug the USB stick or monitoring dongle, shut the inverter down, then plug it back in. If the code stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The inverter cannot talk to the energy meter.
codes.action: Check that the meter is powered and that its cable to the inverter is connected properly.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.meaning: Output high DCI (DC injection in AC output)
codes.causes: Too much DC current is appearing in the AC output.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage reading is faulty.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The settings memory (EEPROM) is not working properly.
codes.action: Restart. If the warning stays, Growatt service replaces the control (M3) board.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: A grid relay inside the inverter has failed its check.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The firmware versions on the inverter's boards do not match.
codes.action: The firmware needs updating to the matching version by the installer or Growatt service.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The inverter's automatic self-test did not pass.
codes.action: Restart and run the self-test again; if it still fails, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The inverter is too hot.
codes.action: Improve ventilation and shade first. If the surrounding air is below about 60 °C, restart; if the code stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage is too high.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.meaning: DSP communicates with M3 abnormal (internal communication)
codes.causes: The two control processors inside the inverter cannot communicate.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The settings memory (EEPROM) has failed.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The two processors that measure the same values disagree.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The earth-leakage (GFCI) protection has tripped or failed.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt or the installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

codes.causes: The arc-fault detector failed its own self-test.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Growatt or the installer.
codes.source_ref: Growatt MIN 2500-6000TL-X User Manual GR-UM-155-A-04, sections 11.2 System fault, 11.3 Inverter warning, 11.4 Inverter fault (pp. 37-40)

brands.name: Huawei SUN2000 (L1 single-phase residential)
brands.heading: Huawei SUN2000 L1
brands.models: SUN2000-2KTL-L1 to 6KTL-L1 (alarm IDs are shared across SUN2000 families per Huawei, but only the L1 manual was read)
brands.manual_note: English Issue 10 (2022-10-27) PDF copy; Huawei's official download area is solar.huawei.com (hosts other-language editions, e.g. https://solar.huawei.com/-/media/Solar/attachment/pdf/eu/service/download/SUN2000-2-6KTL-L1-UserManual-GR.pdf). Newer editions exist (Issue 20, 2024-05-30; Edition 24 ES, 2026-01-30) and were not read.

codes.meaning: PV string open-circuit voltage exceeds the inverter maximum (too many modules in series)
codes.causes: Too many panels are connected in series, so the string's open-circuit voltage is above what the inverter can take. The cause ID shows which input (1 = PV1, 2 = PV2).
codes.action: Installer work: re-check the string design so its open-circuit voltage stays below the inverter's maximum input voltage.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.meaning: Electric arc on PV string cables
codes.causes: The solar string cables are arcing or have a poor connection.
codes.action: Do not touch the DC wiring; the installer has to check the string cables and connectors.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.meaning: PV string connected with reversed polarity
codes.causes: A solar string is connected with its plus and minus reversed.
codes.action: Installer work: wait until the string current falls to a very low value, switch the DC isolator off, then correct the polarity.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The arc-fault detection circuit failed its check or is faulty.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.meaning: No grid (outage or AC breaker off)
codes.causes: There is no grid: a power cut (load-shedding), or the AC circuit is disconnected or its breaker is off.
codes.action: Check for load-shedding and that the inverter's AC breaker is on, and check the AC voltage.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The grid voltage is below the inverter's lower limit, or has stayed low longer than its low-voltage ride-through time.
codes.action: If it happens now and then, the grid dipped and the inverter recovers on its own. If it is frequent, check the grid voltage; if the grid is out of range contact the DISCO. Protection limits may only be changed with the DISCO's consent.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The grid voltage is above the inverter's upper limit, or has stayed high longer than its high-voltage ride-through time.
codes.action: Same as 2033: occasional means wait; frequent means check the grid voltage and its peaks and contact the DISCO. Limits change only with the DISCO's consent.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The grid frequency is higher than the local grid standard allows.
codes.action: Occasional: the inverter recovers by itself. Frequent: check the grid frequency and contact the DISCO if it is out of range.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The grid frequency is lower than the local grid standard allows.
codes.action: Occasional: the inverter recovers by itself. Frequent: check the grid frequency and contact the DISCO.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The grid frequency is changing faster than the local grid standard allows.
codes.action: Occasional: the inverter recovers by itself. Frequent: check the grid frequency and contact the DISCO.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: A sharp grid voltage drop or a short circuit on the grid made the output current jump past the inverter's limit, so its protection tripped.
codes.action: The inverter recovers once the grid is normal. If it happens often and costs energy, have the output checked for a short circuit; if it stays, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.meaning: Too much DC in AC output
codes.causes: The DC part of the inverter's output current is above its limit.
codes.action: The inverter normally recovers on its own; if it is frequent, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The insulation between the solar input side and earth has dropped while running, so residual current is too high.
codes.action: Occasional: a passing external fault, the inverter recovers by itself. Frequent or constant: the installer should measure the string-to-earth resistance.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.meaning: PV array insulation to ground too low
codes.causes: The solar array is shorted to earth, or damp weather has lowered its insulation to earth.
codes.action: Installer work: measure the array's resistance to earth and check the inverter's earth (PE) cable. It often shows after rain; if the resistance is only low in wet weather, the installer can adjust the insulation protection setting in the app.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The inverter is too hot: poor ventilation, a hot room, or the unit itself not working properly.
codes.action: Improve ventilation and cooling. If ventilation and temperature are fine and it stays, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.meaning: Unrecoverable internal fault (Cause ID 1-12: boost short/overcurrent, control circuit, inverter circuit, residual current sensor, temperature detection, EEPROM, auxiliary power, grid-tied relay, DC bus over/under-voltage/imbalance)
codes.causes: An internal circuit has a fault the inverter cannot clear by itself (the cause ID names the circuit).
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: A firmware upgrade did not finish, or the software and hardware versions do not match.
codes.action: Run the upgrade again; if it keeps failing, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The monitoring unit's flash memory is full or damaged.
codes.action: Switch off the AC and DC switches, wait five minutes and switch them on. If it stays, the monitoring board needs replacing by the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The smart power sensor (meter) is not connected.
codes.action: Check that the meter model set in the inverter matches the meter fitted, that the communication settings match, and that the meter is powered and its RS485 cable connected.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.meaning: Battery fault, disconnected or breaker off (hybrid/LUNA systems)
codes.causes: The battery is faulty or disconnected, or its breaker is off while the system is running.
codes.action: If the battery's fault light is on or blinking, contact the battery supplier. Otherwise have the installer check the battery's power, enable and communication cables and that its auxiliary switch is on, then shut down from the app and switch on the battery, AC and DC switches in turn after five minutes. If it stays, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The inverter has detected a grid outage and stopped exporting (anti-islanding protection).
codes.action: Usually load-shedding: wait for the grid to return and check the grid voltage at the inverter.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The backup (off-grid) output is overloaded or short-circuited.
codes.action: Switch off loads on the backup circuit and check that the backup load is within the rated power and has no short circuit.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The panel or optimizer layout does not meet the inverter's rules, or a module output is reversed or shorted.
codes.action: Installer work: check the number of modules in total and per string, the number of strings, and the module polarity.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: One of the optimizers is faulty.
codes.action: Open the optimizer screen in the app to see which one and why, and have the installer replace it.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

codes.causes: The inverter cannot communicate with the Smart Backup Box, or the box has an internal fault.
codes.action: Shut down from the app, switch off the AC, DC and battery switches, have the installer check the power and RS485 cables between the box and the inverter, and restart after five minutes. If it stays, contact the dealer or Huawei support.
codes.source_ref: SUN2000-(2KTL-6KTL)-L1 User Manual Issue 10 (2022-10-27), 8.3 Troubleshooting, Table 8-2 Common alarms and troubleshooting measures (pp. 82-94)

brands.name: Solis (Ginlong) on-grid and hybrid
brands.heading: Solis on-grid and hybrid
brands.models: Solis 1P/3P string inverters and RHI/S5/S6 hybrids (article is Solis' complete display-message list; hybrid battery codes not extracted)
brands.manual_note: Manufacturer support article (Solis North America / Ginlong), fetched 2026-10-13; it links the PDF 'Alarm Codes for Solis 1P _ 3P.pdf'.

codes.causes: The grid voltage has been above the first overvoltage limit of the selected grid standard for too long. The variants (01 to 05) cover a short spike, a ten-minute average and a second, higher limit.
codes.action: If it happens once in a while the grid was briefly out of range and the inverter reconnects on its own. If it is frequent, check the grid voltage and frequency, the grid standard set in the inverter, and the AC breaker and output cable. Protection limits may only be changed by Solis service after the DISCO approves.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The grid voltage is below the limit.
codes.action: Same as OV-G-V: wait if occasional; if frequent, check the grid, the wiring and the protection settings.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The grid frequency is above the limit.
codes.action: Same as OV-G-V.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The grid frequency is below the limit.
codes.action: Same as OV-G-V.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: Current is flowing back from the AC side into the inverter.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The inverter cannot detect the grid.
codes.action: Check for load-shedding and that the AC breaker is on, that the grid is connected and normal, and that the right grid standard is set. If the grid is fine and it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The three grid phases are unbalanced.
codes.action: Check that the grid is connected properly and is normal; if it is, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The grid frequency is fluctuating abnormally.
codes.action: Check that the grid is connected and normal; if it is, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The output current to the grid is too high.
codes.action: Check that the grid is connected and normal; if it is, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The inverter cannot track the grid current correctly.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The grid phase angle is abnormal.
codes.action: Have the installer check the AC wiring and that the phases are 120 degrees apart, then restart. If it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The solar (DC) input voltage is too high.
codes.action: Installer work: check that the string voltage is below the inverter's maximum input, then restart. If it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The DC boost circuit has a fault.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage is too high.
codes.action: Have the input voltage checked against the maximum, restart, and contact Solis service if it stays.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The internal DC bus and its half-voltage point do not match (bus unbalanced).
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage is too low.
codes.action: Check whether the input voltage is too low and restart; if it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The DC input current is abnormal.
codes.action: Have the installer check the DC wiring for wrong or damaged connections, then restart. If it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: A DC input is connected with reversed polarity.
codes.action: Installer work: check the DC polarity and cable size and the grid standard setting, then restart. If it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.meaning: PV mid-point low insulation / PV grounded during operation
codes.causes: The insulation at the PV mid-point is low, or a PV terminal is touching earth while running.
codes.action: Installer work. In early morning or after rain it is usually moisture and clears by itself. Otherwise the installer measures each string's resistance to earth (it should be above about 20 kilo-ohm), checks neutral to earth and the software version, then contacts Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The grid voltage waveform is distorted, often where several inverters share one line.
codes.action: The installer may need grid filter settings or to repair equipment downstream, then restart. If it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The control processor failed to start up properly.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The temperature near the power switches is above its limit (around 90 °C on single-phase and 115 °C on three-phase units).
codes.action: Check the unit is not in direct sun and has the clearance the manual asks for, lower the room temperature, switch off and restart after fifteen minutes. If it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The insulation of the solar array to earth is too low.
codes.action: Installer work. In early morning, late afternoon or rain it is often normal moisture. Otherwise the installer measures each string's resistance to earth (above about 20 kilo-ohm), checks neutral to earth, updates the software, then contacts Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: Leakage current to earth is too high. Typical causes: damaged PV cable insulation, wrong cable size, a faulty transformer downstream, wrong rapid-shutdown wiring, wet buried AC cables or poor AC cable; in rain or early morning, ageing panels.
codes.action: Installer work: connect the strings one at a time to find the faulty one. Solis support can sometimes fix it with a remote software update.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The grid relay failed its self-check. The source lists the code without a solution.
codes.action: Restart; if it stays, contact Solis service, as for other internal faults.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The internal or external cooling fan has a fault.
codes.action: Check the fan is not blocked; a replacement is installer work.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: A surge on the grid was recorded for service records; it does not stop the inverter.
codes.action: No action needed.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

codes.causes: The AC surge protection device has a fault.
codes.action: Restart the inverter; if it stays, contact Solis service.
codes.source_ref: Solis North America support article 'Solis Inverter Alarm Codes (Complete List)', section 'Alarm Messages (ordered by Alarm Code)'

brands.name: GoodWe (ES Uniq hybrid; F-codes are shared across GoodWe residential inverters)
brands.heading: GoodWe ES Uniq hybrid
brands.models: GW ES Uniq 8-12K with LX A/U batteries (manual read); on-grid DNS/MS/SDT and other hybrids (ET/EH) use the same F01-F163 numbering per this manual's 'all PV inverters' wording - verify per model
brands.manual_note: Official GoodWe manual from en.goodwe.com, V2.9 dated 2026-10-10. Only F01-F39 extracted; F41-F163 (battery, BMS, backup) not extracted in the time box.

codes.causes: There is no grid: a power cut, or the AC cable or AC switch is disconnected.
codes.action: The code clears by itself when the grid returns. Check for load-shedding and that the AC switch and cable are connected.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The grid voltage is above the allowed range, or has stayed high longer than the high-voltage ride-through time.
codes.action: If it happens now and then, the grid was briefly out of range and the inverter reconnects on its own. If it is frequent, check the grid voltage; if it is out of range, contact the DISCO. If it does not clear for a long time, check the AC breaker and output cable.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The grid voltage is below the allowed range, or has stayed low longer than the low-voltage ride-through time.
codes.action: If it happens now and then, the grid was briefly out of range and the inverter reconnects on its own. If it is frequent, check the grid voltage; if it is out of range, contact the DISCO. If it does not clear for a long time, check the AC breaker and output cable.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: A sudden very high grid voltage, or a fault in the grid voltage measurement, tripped the inverter.
codes.action: If it happens now and then, the grid was briefly out of range and the inverter reconnects on its own. If it is frequent, check the grid voltage; if it is out of range, contact the DISCO. If it does not clear for a long time, check the AC breaker and output cable.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The grid voltage averaged over ten minutes is above the limit of the grid standard.
codes.action: Check whether the grid voltage stays high for long periods; if it does, contact the DISCO.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The grid frequency is above the local grid standard.
codes.action: Occasional: the inverter reconnects by itself. Frequent: check the grid frequency and contact the DISCO. Protection limits change only with the DISCO's consent.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The grid frequency is below the local grid standard.
codes.action: Same as F06.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The grid frequency is changing faster than the local grid standard allows.
codes.action: Occasional: the inverter reconnects by itself. Frequent: contact the DISCO.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.meaning: Grid lost but voltage held by load; inverter stops grid connection
codes.causes: The grid has gone off but connected loads are holding up the voltage, so the inverter stops exporting as safety rules require.
codes.action: Occasional: the inverter reconnects by itself. Frequent: contact the DISCO.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.meaning: Grid voltage abnormal longer than ride-through time
codes.causes: The grid voltage stayed abnormal longer than the ride-through time.
codes.action: Occasional: the inverter reconnects by itself. Frequent: check that grid voltage and frequency are in range and stable; if not, contact the DISCO.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.code: F12 / F13 / F14 / F15 GFCI Protection (30mA / 60mA / 150mA / slow change)
codes.causes: Leakage current to earth tripped the inverter (the levels shown are the trip thresholds) because the insulation of the input side to earth dropped while running.
codes.action: Occasional: a passing external fault, the inverter recovers by itself. Frequent or lasting: the installer should check the PV string-to-earth resistance.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.meaning: DC component in AC output too high
codes.causes: The DC part of the inverter's output current is above the allowed limit.
codes.action: If an external fault caused it, the inverter recovers by itself. If it is frequent and cuts generation, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.meaning: PV or battery insulation to ground too low
codes.causes: The PV string or battery port is shorted to earth, or long damp weather has lowered the insulation to earth.
codes.action: Installer work: measure the string and battery port resistance to earth and find any short, and check the inverter's earth conductor. If the resistance is only low in rainy weather, the installer can adjust the insulation protection point in the app.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The inverter's protective earth is not connected, or a grounded PV string is used without an isolation transformer on the output.
codes.action: Installer work: connect the protective earth properly; with a grounded PV string, fit an isolation transformer on the output.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The load is fluctuating abnormally.
codes.action: If an external cause, the inverter recovers by itself; if frequent, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: An internal chip is not powered or has the wrong firmware, so internal communication timed out.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.code: F22-F27 Generator faults (waveform, abnormal connection, voltage low/high, frequency low/high)
codes.causes: The generator input is outside its limits. This shows all the time when no generator is connected.
codes.action: With no generator connected, ignore it. With a generator it clears by itself once the generator runs normally; off-grid operation is not affected.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: A parallel communication cable is loose or the parallel I/O chip is damaged.
codes.action: Installer work: secure the parallel communication cable; if the chip is damaged it must be replaced.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.meaning: Grid wires reversed between parallel units
codes.causes: Some parallel units have their grid wires reversed compared with the others.
codes.action: Installer work: reconnect the grid wires correctly.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The AC current sensor reading is abnormal.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The leakage-current sensor reading is abnormal.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The inverter has detected an internal fault.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The internal flash memory changed unexpectedly or is worn out.
codes.action: Update to the latest firmware; if it stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The arc-fault module did not detect the test arc during its self-check.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.causes: The inverter is too hot: poor ventilation, a hot room, or the internal fan not working.
codes.action: Improve ventilation and keep the room within the allowed temperature. If both are fine and it stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.meaning: Internal DC bus voltage too high
codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage is too high, from a high PV voltage or a measurement or transformer problem.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.meaning: PV string voltage above inverter maximum
codes.causes: Too many panels are connected in series, so the string's open-circuit voltage is above the inverter's maximum.
codes.action: Installer work: re-design the string so its open-circuit voltage stays below the maximum; the alarm clears once it is correct.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

codes.code: F38 / F39 PV Continuous Hardware / Software Overcurrent
codes.causes: The PV input current is too high, from a wrong module configuration or damaged hardware.
codes.action: Switch off the AC output switch and the DC input switch, wait five minutes and switch them back on. If the fault stays, contact the dealer or GoodWe service.
codes.source_ref: GoodWe Residential Smart Inverter Solutions User Manual (ES Uniq 8-12K, LX A/U batteries) V2.9 2026-10-10, 9.5.2.2.1 Fault Handling (Fault Codes F01-F40), pp. 266-283

brands.name: Sungrow SG RS single-phase on-grid
brands.heading: Sungrow SG RS on-grid
brands.models: SG2.0RS-S / 2.5RS-S / 3.0RS-S / 3.0RS / 3.6RS / 4.0RS / 5.0RS / 6.0RS (manual says the code table covers 'all PV inverters' but only some apply per model)
brands.manual_note: Official Sungrow manual from info-support.sungrowpower.com, Ver21 (2023-12).

codes.causes: The grid voltage is above the protection setting. The inverter normally reconnects once the grid is back to normal.
codes.action: If it repeats, measure the grid voltage and contact the DISCO if it is above the setting, and have the protection settings checked in the app or display. Limits change only with the DISCO's consent. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The grid voltage is below the protection setting. The inverter normally reconnects once the grid is back to normal.
codes.action: If it repeats, measure the grid voltage and contact the DISCO, have the protection settings and the AC cable checked. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The grid frequency is above the protection setting. The inverter normally reconnects by itself.
codes.action: If it repeats, measure the grid frequency and contact the DISCO if it is out of range, and have the protection settings checked. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The grid frequency is below the protection setting. The inverter normally reconnects by itself.
codes.action: Same as 008.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: There is no grid. The inverter reconnects when the grid returns.
codes.action: Check for load-shedding and that the AC breaker is on; the installer checks that the AC cable is tight and live and neutral are on the right terminals. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: Leakage current is too high, often from weak sunlight or a damp setting; the inverter usually reconnects when conditions improve.
codes.action: If conditions are normal and it stays, the installer should check the insulation of the AC and DC cables. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: A grid value is outside the set range. The inverter normally reconnects by itself.
codes.action: Measure the grid and contact the DISCO if it is out of range. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: On a three-phase supply, the phase voltages differ too much. The inverter normally reconnects by itself.
codes.action: Measure the phase voltages and contact the DISCO if they differ a lot; the installer can adjust the imbalance setting. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: A PV string is connected with reversed polarity (the code number shows which input or string).
codes.action: Installer work: switch the DC isolator off once the string current is very low and correct the polarity. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The inverter or its power module is too hot; it restarts once the temperature is normal.
codes.action: Check that the room is not too hot, the unit is well ventilated and out of direct sun (shade it if not), and that the fan runs; a dead fan is replaced. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.meaning: PV/battery insulation to ground too low
codes.causes: The insulation of the system to earth is too low.
codes.action: Installer work. Wait for the inverter to recover; if it repeats, check the insulation protection setting, measure the string and DC cable resistance to earth, re-check in dry weather if it only happens in rain, and check the battery cables. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The room is too cold for the inverter to run, so it stops.
codes.action: It restarts when the temperature is back within its operating range.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The parallel communication cable or its terminals have a problem.
codes.action: Installer work: check and reconnect the communication cable. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.code: 084 Reverse Connection Alarm of the Meter/CT
codes.meaning: Energy meter or CT wired backwards
codes.causes: The energy meter or current sensor (CT) is wired wrongly or reversed.
codes.action: Installer work: check the meter wiring and its input and output direction, and the rated power setting where an existing inverter is also connected.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: An electric arc was detected on the DC side.
codes.action: Installer work: switch the DC supply off and check for damaged DC cables and loose terminals or fuses, then switch back on and clear the fault in the app or display. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The earth cable has a problem.
codes.action: Installer work: check the AC cable connections and the insulation between earth and live. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: An MPPT input is connected with reversed polarity.
codes.action: Installer work: switch the DC isolator off once the string current is very low and correct the polarity; otherwise contact Sungrow.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.meaning: Output port connected to a live grid when it should not be
codes.causes: The inverter's output port is connected to a live grid where it should not be.
codes.action: Installer work: disconnect the output from the grid. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The boost capacitor voltage is too high. As an alarm (332-363) the inverter keeps running; as a fault (364-395) it stops.
codes.action: Alarm: check the wiring and terminals and for anything foreign in the unit. Fault: switch off AC, DC and any battery switches, wait fifteen minutes, switch on AC and DC in turn and restart. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: The energy meter is not communicating.
codes.action: Check and reconnect the meter's communication cable. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: A PV string has reversed polarity (alarm level; the code shows which string).
codes.action: Same as 028/029.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.meaning: String producing abnormally (shading, loose wiring, fuse)
codes.causes: A PV string is producing less than expected: shading or dirt on its modules, loose wiring or a blown DC fuse.
codes.action: You can check for shade and dirt on the panels; wiring and fuses are installer work. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: A general internal system fault.
codes.action: Wait for the inverter to recover. If not, switch off AC, DC and any battery switches, wait fifteen minutes, switch on AC and DC in turn and restart. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

codes.causes: A general system alarm; the inverter keeps running.
codes.action: Check the related wiring and terminals and look for foreign objects or other problems around the unit, and correct them. Contact Sungrow service if these are fine and the fault keeps coming.
codes.source_ref: Sungrow SG2.0RS-S...SG6.0RS User Manual SG2.0-6.0RS-UEN-Ver21-202312, 9.1 Troubleshooting (pp. 103-109)

brands.name: Fronius (Symo / Primo SnapINverter STATE codes; GEN24 1xxx codes)
brands.heading: Fronius Symo, Primo and GEN24
brands.models: Symo Hybrid (online manual read; Class 1-5 codes are shared with Symo/Primo/Galvo SnapINverters per Fronius numbering) and Primo GEN24 7.7/10.0 (GEN24 lists only 1030/1173/1191 in its manual)
brands.manual_note: Official Fronius online manual manuals.fronius.com (Symo Hybrid, doc 42,0426,0222) read via page fetch; some rows were merged in the HTML table so 406-408 and 459-461 remedies are table-layout inferences. GEN24 PDF is Fronius' own manual hosted by a US distributor.

codes.meaning: AC (grid) voltage too high; class 1 codes = grid conditions outside permissible range
codes.causes: The grid voltage is too high (102). The other class 1 codes in this group cover grid voltage, frequency or islanding conditions outside the allowed range.
codes.action: The inverter waits until the grid has been back in range for a while, then starts again. Check for grid problems; if the code keeps coming back, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.causes: The AC output current was too high.
codes.action: Feed-in stops for a moment and the inverter starts again. If the code stays on permanently, a Fronius-trained technician is needed.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: Overcurrent DC or battery not detected
codes.causes: The DC current is too high, or the battery is not detected.
codes.action: Same as 301.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: DC module overtemperature (PV) / AC module overtemperature
codes.causes: The DC (PV) or AC power module is too hot.
codes.action: Clean the cooling air openings and heat sink. The inverter clears it by itself; if the code keeps coming back, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: No power being fed in, despite closed relays
codes.causes: The relays are closed but no power is being fed in.
codes.action: The inverter clears it by itself; if the code keeps coming back, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: Not enough PV power to feed in (normal at dawn/dusk)
codes.causes: There is not enough solar power to feed in and none is being drawn from the battery. At dawn and dusk this is routine, not a fault.
codes.action: Wait for more sunlight.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: DC input voltage too low to feed in (normal at night)
codes.causes: The DC input voltage is too low to feed in; normal at night.
codes.action: Wait for more sunlight.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.causes: The internal (intermediate circuit) voltage is too high.
codes.action: The inverter clears it by itself; if the code keeps coming back, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: Unable to communicate with the power stage set
codes.causes: The inverter cannot communicate with its power stage.
codes.action: It retries by itself and resumes feeding in when it can. If the code stays permanently, a Fronius-trained technician is needed.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: DC module temperature sensor faulty (PV) / AC module temperature sensor faulty / DC component measured in the grid too high
codes.causes: A temperature sensor on the DC or AC module is faulty (406, 407), or the DC part measured in the grid is too high (408).
codes.action: If the code keeps coming back, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: Fixed voltage mode selected instead of MPP voltage mode
codes.causes: The inverter is set to a fixed input voltage instead of tracking the best (MPP) voltage, and the fixed value is too low or too high.
codes.action: A setting the installer has to correct.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: No communication between power stage set and control system
codes.causes: The power stage and the control system cannot communicate.
codes.action: Same as 401.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: Grid relay sticking or neutral conductor ground voltage too high
codes.causes: A grid relay is sticking, or the neutral-to-earth voltage is too high; the inverter has stopped feeding in.
codes.action: Installer work: check the earthing so the neutral-to-earth voltage stays below 30 V.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: Error recording the measuring signal for the insulation test / DSP reference voltage out of tolerance / DSP data memory error
codes.causes: An internal check failed: the insulation-test measurement, a processor reference voltage or the processor's data memory. The inverter is not feeding in.
codes.action: If the code stays permanently, a service technician is needed.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: Insulation fault on solar modules or on the battery
codes.causes: There is an insulation fault on the solar modules or the battery.
codes.action: If the code keeps coming back, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: No energy fed into the grid in the past 24 hours
codes.causes: No energy has been fed into the grid in the past 24 hours.
codes.action: Acknowledge the code and check that feed-in is possible: DC switch on, panels not shaded, dirty or covered. If all is fine, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.meaning: DC low (PV), no PV voltage available
codes.causes: There is no PV voltage (DC low). At night, or in standby, this is normal.
codes.action: No action at night. In the day, check the DC switch; if it is on, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.causes: Some circuit boards in the inverter are not compatible with each other.
codes.action: The inverter firmware needs updating by the installer or Fronius service.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.causes: Output power is being reduced because the grid voltage is very high.
codes.action: It clears by itself once the grid voltage is back in range; if it keeps coming back, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Symo Hybrid Operating Instructions (online manual 42,0426,0222), Troubleshooting: 'Status codes - Class 1/3/4/5'

codes.causes: The wired shutdown (WSD) chain is open: a connected device such as a surge protector broke the signal line, or the factory bypass was removed without fitting a trigger device.
codes.action: Installer work: if the surge protector tripped, an authorised specialist must repair the inverter; otherwise refit the bypass or a trigger device, or set the WSD switch to position 1 (primary device).
codes.source_ref: Fronius Primo GEN24 208-240 7.7/10.0 Operating Instructions 42,0426,0312,EA 017-04092025, 'Status codes and remedy' (p. 133)

codes.meaning: Repeated DC arc detected; max auto-reconnects reached
codes.causes: An electric arc was detected on the PV system and the inverter has used up its automatic restarts for the day.
codes.action: Do not just clear it: the whole affected PV system must first be checked for damage, and damaged parts repaired by qualified specialists. Only then is the status confirmed (sensor held three seconds, or in the event log).
codes.source_ref: Fronius Primo GEN24 208-240 7.7/10.0 Operating Instructions 42,0426,0312,EA 017-04092025, 'Status codes and remedy' (p. 133)

codes.causes: An electric arc was detected on the PV system (information only).
codes.action: No action needed by itself; if it repeats it becomes 1173.
codes.source_ref: Fronius Primo GEN24 208-240 7.7/10.0 Operating Instructions 42,0426,0312,EA 017-04092025, 'Status codes and remedy' (p. 133)

brands.name: Voltronic Power Axpert (base design of many Pakistani rebrands)
brands.heading: Voltronic Axpert
brands.models: Axpert VM III 1.5/3/5 kW (manual read). Other Axpert families (VM IV, MKS IV, MAX, MAX II, King) use the same 01-09 / 51-59 numbering with model-specific additions (MAX II adds 11 PV over voltage, 12 DC/DC over current, 13 battery discharge over current, per voltronicpower.com manual listing - not read). Pakistani brands sold as 'Axpert'-type units (e.g. Inverex Axpert, Ziewnic Axpert) are widely reported to be Voltronic OEM units, but no Inverex/Knox manual was fetched to confirm their code tables.
brands.manual_note: Official Voltronic manual from voltronicpower.com (v1.8, 2020-09-04). Other official Axpert manuals: https://voltronicpower.com/content/download/Manual/Axpert%20VM%20IV-4K6K-TWIN-Off-grid-manual-20220629.pdf , https://voltronicpower.com/content/download/Manual/Axpert%20MAX%20II-manual-20210811.pdf

codes.causes: The cooling fan has failed.
codes.action: Clean dust from the fan; if it does not turn, the installer replaces it.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: A part inside the inverter is too hot (above about 100 to 120 °C).
codes.action: Make sure air can flow around the unit and the room is not too hot.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: The battery is over-charged or its voltage is too high.
codes.action: Have the installer check that the battery type, number of batteries and charge settings suit the inverter; otherwise the unit needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: The battery voltage is too low (below about 1.91 V per cell at start-up).
codes.action: Recharge the battery; if it will not hold charge, it needs replacing.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: The output is short-circuited, or an internal part has overheated.
codes.action: Switch the loads off and look for a faulty appliance or wiring fault; if it stays, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.meaning: Output voltage too high / too low
codes.causes: The output voltage is outside its normal band (below about 190 V or above about 260 V).
codes.action: Reduce the load. If it repeats, the unit needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: The load has been above about 110% of the rating for too long. A PV voltage above the specification also reduces output power and can cause this.
codes.action: Switch some appliances off; if the PV voltage is too high, the installer reduces the number of panels in series.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.meaning: Bus voltage too high / bus soft start failed / inverter soft start failed / current sensor failed
codes.causes: An internal component has failed.
codes.action: The unit needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: An over-current or surge was detected.
codes.action: Restart the unit; if the code comes back, it needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: The internal DC bus voltage is too low.
codes.action: Restart the unit; if the code comes back, it needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.meaning: Over DC voltage in AC output / output voltage unbalanced

codes.action: Restart the unit; if the code comes back, it needs the service centre.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.causes: The PV input voltage is above the specification.
codes.action: Installer work: reduce the number of panels in series.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III User Manual v1.8, 'TROUBLE SHOOTING' table (p. 43)

codes.meaning: Fan is locked when inverter is on (beep three times every second)

codes.causes: The display panel is not communicating.
codes.action: Check the display cable; if it stays, call the installer.
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III 1.5KW/3KW/5KW User Manual v1.8, 'Fault Reference Code' and 'Warning Indicator' tables (p. 39)

codes.meaning: Battery is not connected / Battery equalization
codes.causes: The battery is disconnected; the relay may click on and off repeatedly.
codes.action: Check that the battery cables are connected tightly (switch off first).
codes.source_ref: Voltronic Axpert VM III 1.5KW/3KW/5KW User Manual v1.8, 'Fault Reference Code' and 'Warning Indicator' tables (p. 39)
